title: Agent-guided construction of Feynman integral bases
abstract: Finding bases of Feynman integrals whose differential equations are suitable for phenomenology is a remarkably verifiable task. We exploit this to design two \emph{skills} with which Claude Opus~5.5 produces novel results autonomously, working for several days. For a two-loop five-point family (with two masses and 18 elliptic sectors) and a two-loop superfamily for the radiative jet function with a K3 sector, the agent finds bases whose differential equations are free of poles in the dimensional regulator $\varepsilon$ and at most quadratic in it, and takes the jet-function one to $\varepsilon$-factorized form.

title: The cosmological lithium problem and how decaying relics still solve it
abstract: Lithium-7 in old stars is about three times below the prediction of standard big-bang nucleosynthesis, and deuterium lies slightly above it. Precise measurements of deuterium, helium-4, and the effective number of neutrino species now disfavor most previously proposed particle solutions. We find that relics that decay or evaporate with lifetimes of a few hours, mostly into electron antineutrinos of about a hundred MeV and into electrons or photons, still lower lithium-7 while respecting these measurements. Such relics include gauge bosons of $L_e-L_\tau$ or $B-3L_e$ and heavy neutral leptons with a dipole coupling or mixing with $\nu_\tau$, with masses of a few hundred MeV, and populations of evaporating Q-balls that carry lepton number. The decaying particles substantially alleviate the lithium problem, while Q-ball populations reach the $2\sigma$ range of lithium-7 adopted by the Particle Data Group. These relics can shift the effective number of neutrino species by up to about $2.5$ times the precision expected from the Simons Observatory, and a future Galactic supernova can test the particles.

title: Moment bounds and UV reconstruction from curved positivity cones
abstract: The fundamental principles of the S-matrix impose positivity bounds on the Wilson coefficients of EFTs, including the SMEFT. These bounds form convex cones that often have curved boundaries when there are degeneracies among the irreducible two-particle low-energy states. Numerical approximations have previously been used to evaluate these curved cones. We develop a moment-based framework to analytically carve out these cones, particularly those associated with anomalous quartic gauge couplings in the SMEFT. The framework also allows us to reverse engineer UV models from the curved boundaries of the positivity cones.

title: Dijet production in $e^+e^-$ collisions at NNLO+PS accuracy
abstract: We present the first complete Monte Carlo event generator with next-to-next-to-leading order QCD accuracy for lepton collisions. The approach is based on a new formulation of the MiNNLO formalism and is applied to dijet production. Starting from the resummation of the three-jet resolution variable $y_3$, we present the corresponding MiNNLO master formula and implement it within the Powheg framework. We discuss phenomenological results relevant for LEP and future electron-positron colliders.

title: Exploring Screening Masses of Light and Heavy Spin-$3/2$ Baryons in a Symmetry Preserving Contact Interaction Model
abstract: We present a study of the screening masses of spin-$3/2$ baryons within a symmetry preserving contact interaction framework. Extending previous finite-temperature investigations of light baryons, we analyze 16 systems composed of $u$, $s$, $c$, and $b$ quarks, including light, heavy-light, and fully-heavy configurations with both positive and negative parity states. Whenever available, our results are compared with previous contact interaction calculations and other theoretical predictions. Our analysis shows that the screening masses generally increase with temperature, while the thermal evolution of the relative splitting between positive and negative parity states exhibits a clear dependence on the flavor content. Although a reduction of the relative parity splitting is observed in most channels, this behavior is not universal. Nevertheless, the uncertainties associated with the screening masses allow the parity partners to approach more closely at high temperatures, remaining compatible with an enhanced tendency toward parity degeneracy. Thermal modifications are strongest in the light sector and become increasingly suppressed as the heavy-quark content grows. To characterize this evolution, we introduce characteristic temperatures associated with the onset of thermal effects and find a general tendency for strong thermal modifications to occur at comparable or slightly higher temperatures in the negative parity channel. We further analyze the corresponding Faddeev amplitudes and show that the dominant diquark correlations remain clearly identifiable throughout the temperature range considered. These results provide a unified description of light and heavy spin-$3/2$ baryons and offer new insight into the flavor dependence of their thermal evolution and the persistence of quark--diquark correlations in hot QCD matter.

title: Parity-violating optical rotation in the Th-229 nuclear clock transition
abstract: The exceptionally low-energy nuclear transition in $^{229}$Th provides a new opportunity to study hadronic parity violation (PV) by optical methods. The PV nucleon--nucleus interaction admixes opposite-parity nuclear states into the $5/2^+$ ground state and the $3/2^+$ isomer, thereby inducing an electric-dipole amplitude $E1_{\rm PV}$ that interferes with the magnetic-dipole clock transition amplitude $M1$. In a single-valence-neutron Nilsson model, we find $|E1_{\rm PV}/M1| \sim 2\times10^{-5}$. This interference can be detected as a parity-violating nuclear optical rotation (PVNOR) of resonant laser light transmitted through a $^{229}$Th-doped crystal. For a highly-doped CaF$_2$ crystal fiber, the estimated rotation is of order $10^{-6}\,{\rm rad}$. A crossed-polarizer measurement can reach this sensitivity with existing ultraviolet laser technology. We also analyze systematic effects in the form of optical birefringence, stray magnetic-field-induced Faraday rotation, and local crystal defects. Such a measurement would provide the first direct probe of the PV neutron-nucleus interaction constant, $g_n$.

title: A relativistic von K\'arm\'an relation for assessing applicability of hydrodynamics
abstract: Relativistic viscous hydrodynamics is a widely used theoretical framework for simulating quark-gluon plasma (QGP) dynamics in relativistic heavy-ion collisions. One open question is how to quantitatively assess the validity of a hydrodynamic description of such a system. In this work, we extract the poles of linear response functions from numerical simulations of hydrodynamics and Boltzmann transport. By comparing these responses as a function of the rescaled wavenumber $\bar{k}$, we identify the wavenumber range over which hydrodynamics captures the underlying microscopic dynamics. We show that the averaged Knudsen number, $\langle\mathrm{Kn}^{*}\rangle$, which we define using the von K\'arm\'an relation, serves as a measure of $\bar{k}$. We find that $\langle\mathrm{Kn}^{*}\rangle_{\rm max}\sim 1$ marks the approximate upper limit of agreement between the linear responses of second-order viscous hydrodynamics and Boltzmann transport.

title: Study of Radiative Muon Capture Experimental Data and its Implications for Muon-Conversion Experiments
abstract: Radiative muon capture (RMC) is an important background in searches for the neutrinoless conversion of a muon into an electron in the field of a nucleus, and in particular in searches for the lepton flavor and lepton number violating process of muon-to-positron conversion. The high-energy tail of the RMC photon spectrum remains theoretically understudied, leading to large uncertainties in background predictions for upcoming muon-conversion experiments. In this work, we revisit previously published RMC data to investigate improved modeling of the high-energy tail. We develop a model characterized by distinct nucleon-knockout final states, each with its associated multibody phase space and kinematic endpoint. This framework is applied to photon data from TRIUMF and positron data from SINDRUM II, and the results are compared to the previously used closure approximation. We find that separately modeling the distinct nucleon-knockout final states provides an improved description of the available RMC data near the endpoint, and we discuss the implications for the COMET and Mu2e experiments.

title: Unstable particle collisions in space and time
abstract: A proper quantum description of colliding beams reveals the spacetime structure of collision processes, going beyond the conventional picture of classical point-like particles undergoing short-distance scattering. This familiar picture emerges as an approximation in the classical beam limit and under specific conditions. Resolving the t-channel singularity in processes initiated by an unstable particle requires going beyond the short-distance treatment because this singularity is associated with a long-distance effect: the decay of the unstable particle, followed by the propagation of its decay products until they scatter with the other beam. In this article, we develop the theory of spacetime collisions to allow the systematic study of the classical expansion accessing quantum corrections, and we apply it to unstable-particle collisions. At all orders in the expansion, we find that long-distance effects associated with unstable-particle decay coexist with direct short-distance interactions with the other beam. At leading order, the short-distance component is described by a cross section. This allows us to define and compute the unstable-particle scattering cross section through a uniquely specified regularization prescription for the t-channel singularity. Prospective applications include cross-section calculations for muon experiments, including a muon collider. It would also be interesting to design experiments to observe the novel effects arising from the quantum nature of the colliding beams that emerge in our formalism.

title: Evidence for Y-shaped color confinement of fully heavy baryons
abstract: The geometry of color confinement in baryons remains a fundamental question in quantum chromodynamics. We investigate whether heavy-quark spectroscopy can distinguish a genuine three-body Y-shaped confining interaction from a sum of pairwise $\Delta$-shaped interaction. Using a high-precision three-body Schr\"odinger solver, we perform a simultaneous analysis of experimentally measured bottomonium masses and lattice-QCD calculations of $\Omega_{bbb}$ excitation energies. For each confinement scenario, interaction parameters are independently optimized against the combined spectra. We find that the Y-shaped potential provides a consistent description of both systems, whereas the $\Delta$-shaped potential exhibits significant discrepancies. Our results provide spectroscopic evidence favoring a collective three-body confining interaction and establish triply-heavy baryon spectroscopy as a complementary probe of the nonperturbative geometry of color confinement.

title: Computing the Wave: Bridging Gravitational Wave and High-Energy-Physics software (with modular ROOT extensions)
authors: Marco Meyer-Conde (on behalf of the LIGO Scientific
Hirotaka Takahashi (on behalf of the LIGO Scientific
Nobuyuki Kanda (on behalf of the LIGO Scientific
Ken-ichi Oohara (on behalf of the LIGO Scientific
Kazuki Sakai (on behalf of the LIGO Scientific
abstract: High-Energy Physics (HEP) and Gravitational Wave (GW) astronomy pursue different scientific goals, yet they face strikingly similar computing challenges and can enrich one another through shared software. Building on the prototype presented at ACAT 2024, we report on the consolidation of that work into a single, modular extension of the CERN ROOT data-analysis framework, freely distributed under RIOPlus. The library is now organised as a set of optional, dynamically loadable extensions covering configuration and file-format parsing (including the Gravitational Wave Frame (GWF) format and HDF5), remote and federated data access (OSDF/Pelican, S3, Kafka) with token-based credentials, an enhanced dynamic-display manager, an advanced signal-processing layer built on the KFR library, and a complex-capable tensor layer backed by LibTorch with ONNX interoperability. We summarise the design of each extension, outline the intended application to transient-noise (glitch) detection and classification, and update the FFT performance benchmark comparing KFR with FFTW. We close with the end-to-end ROOT-centred workflow these extensions enable, its current status, and an outlook toward column-wise RNTuple storage.

title: Weight-space programming and mechanistic interpretability for model editing in particle physics
abstract: We demonstrate that weight-space programming and edits guided by sparse autoencoders can remove unwanted aspects of a particle-physics foundation model through direct edits to its weights. In a foundation model trained on jets, we observe that adding a single soft neutral particle causes large changes in jet classification, violating infrared safety. We locate the responsible attention heads with mechanistic analysis and trace the flaw's origin to pretraining on datasets with different reconstruction thresholds. We then propose two targeted approaches to repair the flaw: by removing three latent directions identified with sparse autoencoders, and by letting language-model agents edit the weights directly, without gradients and with only 50 queries to the model. Both their edits individually remove almost the entire flaw and leave the rest of the model's response nearly unchanged. Compared to fine-tuning, both methods change far fewer parameters. Although built only on $W$ and QCD jets, the edits carry over to all signal classes, the pretrained generator, and a newly trained regression head.

title: Features investigated: A detailed study of axion monodromy inflation using CLiENT
abstract: We investigate features in the primordial power spectrum from inflation, specifically those predicted by the axion monodromy model, using recent observational data. In order to compute posteriors, profile likelihoods and Bayesian evidence accurately for the complex likelihood surfaces arising in this model we have used the CLiENT emulator framework. As our data combinations we use both a "conservative" set consisting of Planck PR4 temperature, polarisation and lensing data together with DESI DR2 BAO and Pantheon+ supernovae, and a more "aggressive" set which also includes small-scale CMB data from ACT and SPT. We find no robust oscillatory feature in current data. With the conservative data the best fit lies at a frequency $\omega \simeq 51$ and lowers $\chi^2$ by 10.1 relative to a featureless spectrum. However, this feature is disfavoured by the more aggressive data combination, whose best fit lies at $\omega \simeq 31$ and lowers $\chi^2$ by 7.4. Fits to featureless data are known to give similar improvements, and the Akaike information criterion, the Bayes factors and the look-elsewhere effect all indicate that neither improvement is significant. The amplitude is limited to $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.056$ and $A_\mathrm{osc} < 0.062$ (95%) for the two datasets. The emulators reproduce the true log-likelihood at samples of their posteriors with rms errors of 0.07 and 0.16, and the profile likelihoods are calculated with the true likelihood, using the profile capability of CLiENT.

title: Electronic Wichmann-Kroll correction to the energy levels of muonic hydrogen-like atoms
abstract: Using modern multiloop calculation methods, we obtain correction to energy levels of muonic hydrogen-like atoms due to the leading-order ($\propto\alpha (Z\alpha)^3$) Wichmann-Kroll electronic potential. Our result is expressed in terms of generalized polylogarithms. As a byproduct, we also obtain the Wichmann-Kroll potential in momentum space in terms of the same functions.

title: A resolution-based framework for coherent and decoherent jet energy loss in NLO pQCD
abstract: We investigate the role of medium resolution and color decoherence in jet energy loss in high-energy heavy-ion collisions. Within an NLO pQCD framework, implemented using NLOJet++, we calculate inclusive jet production in $pp$ collisions and extend the calculation to $AA$ collisions by incorporating nuclear PDFs, Glauber geometry, and medium-induced jet energy loss in the Higher-Twist formalism. To account for the finite resolution of the QGP, we introduce a sequential coherent clustering procedure based on the pairwise invariant mass of final-state partons. The resulting coherent clusters act as independent color sources when resolved by the medium, with the transition governed by an effective resolution scale $Q_{\rm med}$. We validate the coherent clustering procedure using PYTHIA simulations and investigate the nuclear modification factors of inclusive jets, reclustered jets, soft-drop $r_g$, and jet mass in Pb+Pb collisions at $s_{NN}=5.02$ TeV. Comparison with the ATLAS measurements yields $Q_{\rm med}=10-20$ GeV. While coherent energy loss alone systematically underestimates the observed suppression at high jet $p_{\rm T}^{\rm jet}$ and fails to reproduce the substructure dependence of jet quenching, incorporating decoherent energy loss provides a consistent description of these observables. Our results demonstrate that accounting for the medium's ability to resolve jet substructure is essential for a consistent description of jet quenching in heavy-ion collisions at the LHC.

title: Interplay of elliptical laser polarization and scattering geometry in laser-assisted pair production of doubly charged Higgs bosons in the Higgs Triplet Model
abstract: We study the pair production of a doubly charged Higgs boson via $e^{-} e^{+}$ in the presence of a polarized laser field in the Higgs Triplet Model (HTM), mediated by the photon and the $Z$ boson exchange. A unified formulation based on generalized Bessel functions is developed for a monochromatic plane wave with arbitrary ellipticity, encompassing linear, circular, and elliptical polarization states. The numerical analysis shows a strong interplay between laser polarization and scattering geometry, affecting both the characteristic multiphoton domain and the relative strengths of individual harmonic contributions. At a fixed cycle-averaged squared laser potential, the peak ratio normalized to linear polarization exhibits distinct geometry-dependent trends, including a reversal of the polarization hierarchy between different incidence configurations. The dependence on the collision energy and doubly charged Higgs boson mass is also investigated, revealing pronounced kinematic effects on the differential cross section. In contrast, the relative polarization pattern remains similar over a broad mass range. These results provide a unified characterization of polarization and geometrical effects on the multiphoton structure of this process.

title: Mass Spectra and Radiative Decay Widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\)
abstract: Inspired by recent experimental reports on the radiative decay \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma\) and the branching-fraction ratio \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma]\), we investigate the mass spectra and radiative decay widths of \(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^+\), \(D_{s1}(2460)^+\) and \(D_{s1}'(2536)^+\). Within the chiral quark model combined with the Gaussian Expansion Method, the mass spectra obtained agree reasonably well with the experimental data. Besides, the branching-fraction ratio obtained in this work is \(\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma]/\mathcal{B}[D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma] = 0.57\) and \(\Gamma(D_{s0}^{*}(2317)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma) = 3.80\,\mathrm{keV}\). By analyzing our theoretical results against the latest experimental measurements, we conclude that the \(D_{s1}(2460)^{+}\) can be treated as a mixed state of \(1^1P_1\) and \(1^3P_1\), and it may contain both the \(c\bar{s}\) component and the tetraquark component. In addition, we also obtain \(\Gamma(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{*+}\gamma) = 9.14\,\mathrm{keV}\) and \(\Gamma(D'_{s1}(2536)^{+}\to D_s^{+}\gamma) = 8.59\,\mathrm{keV}\) by treating \(D'_{s1}(2536)^+\) as a meson state. More precise experimental data are required to pin down the internal structure of these states.

title: Regularizing gravity in the presence of matter fields
abstract: We investigate how matter fields affect spacetime regularity in a class of gravitational theories with second-order field equations in spherical symmetry, of which general relativity is a special case, and which may encode effective corrections from an underlying quantum theory of gravity. Focusing on spherically symmetric black holes and cosmological spacetimes in theories in which vacuum spacetimes display bounded curvature invariants, we derive the conditions under which regular geometries can be supported by static and perturbative scalar fields, electromagnetic fields, and radiation fluids. We discuss the impact of matter on the regularity requirements of curvature boundedness and geodesic completeness relative to vacuum, finding in general that coupling to matter does not eliminate the existence of theories with regular solutions.

title: Flavor-Modulated Neutrino Communication: Channel Model, Modulation Schemes, and Link Budget for Through-Earth Links
abstract: We investigate the physical limits of transmitting information through the Earth using neutrinos, modeling the link as a discrete-input, Poisson-output classical channel whose crosstalk is set by the three-flavor evolution operator in a layered, matter-filled Earth. For the maximum-likelihood receiver, we derive closed-form Bhattacharyya and Chernoff error exponents for Poisson counts, accurate to within 0.4\% of the exact Chernoff limit. We examine three modulation schemes: source-flavor keying (SFK), oscillation-phase keying (OPK), and matter-path keying (MPK). For an Earth-diameter link with a neutrino-factory-class source (\(3 \times 10^{13}\) decays/s) and a 200 kt detector, the mean charged-current event rate is \(1.31 \times 10^{-2}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\), yet the information rate is only \(1.36 \times 10^{-4}\) bit/s for SFK and \(5.2 \times 10^{-6}\) bit/s for OPK. This reduction occurs because at \(E \simeq 25\) GeV the first oscillation maximum nearly fully relabels \(\nu_\mu \to \nu_\tau\) (\(T_{\mu\tau} \simeq 0.98\)); SFK relies mainly on a count-based \(e\)-like channel, while OPK suffers from suppressed appearance probabilities. For DUNE and T2HK with horn-polarity keying, assuming \(10^{4}\) unoscillated events per year, rates are \(\sim 10^{-6}\)--\(10^{-7}\) bit/s. The OPK estimate is highly sensitive to the Earth density profile: full tabulated PREM lowers it threefold relative to a three-layer model, and a \(\pm 2\%\) density rescaling changes it by an order of magnitude, whereas SFK varies by less than 10\%. Flavor modulation does not remove the fundamental flux limit; it adds a signaling dimension with constant-intensity operation and directional access, though these do not constitute a cryptographic guarantee

title: Probing Compressed Dark Sectors at a Muon Collider through Dilepton Signatures and Machine Learning
abstract: The inert doublet model (IDM), a minimal extension of the Standard Model (SM), provides a scalar dark matter (DM) candidate that belongs to the additional Higgs doublet. The model faces challenges in achieving the correct relic abundance for compressed spectra and DM masses in the high-mass range. In this work we investigate the prospects of detecting dark matter candidates at future high-energy muon colliders. Focusing on the process $\mu^+ \mu^- \to AH$ with subsequent decay $A \to H Z^*$ and $Z^* \to \ell^+\ell^-$, we explore the sensitivity of machine learning techniques, specifically Boosted Decision Trees (BDT) and XGBoost, to distinguish the signal from Standard Model backgrounds. We demonstrate that the combination of advanced multivariate analysis with high-luminosity muon collisions enhances the discovery potential for inert scalars in compressed mass spectra scenarios.

title: nuSTORM: a unique GeV electron-(anti)neutrino machine
abstract: In this conference contribution, I briefly review current experimental programmes measuring the Dirac CP phase {\delta}CP using accelerator neutrinos. I argue that the nuSTORM concept---neutrino beams from a muon storage ring---could provide high-quality electron-(anti)neutrino beams needed for the cross-section inputs to {\delta}CP measurements.

title: Saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at LH$\mu$C
abstract: Motivated by recent proposal of high energy $\mu^+$-hadron collider at CERN, LH$\mu$C, which could be a natural extension of the LH$e$C at the end of the HL-LHC stage, we have studied expected gluon saturation effects in two and three jet production processes at DIS; these processes are sensitive to the most basic non-perturbative structure parametrizing hadronic content of small-$x$ gluons, the Weizs\"acker-Williams (WW) TMD gluon distribution. For the nominal center-of-mass energy of LH$\mu$C $\sqrt{s}=5.3$~TeV we have computed a large selection of observables using the ITMD framework in Mote Carlo setting, both for proton and lead target. In the context of future data-driven precise restrictions of the WW TMD gluon distribution, we have computed several azimuthal angle correlations, including the correlations between pairs of jets as well as the outgoing $\mu^+$ and jet plane. We have also computed nuclear modification factors, that show a significant suppression, ranging locally between 30%-40%, depending on the observable.

title: Probing grand unification in the dark dimension: proton decay and collider signatures
abstract: We study the geometric connection between a stretched grand-unified state, proton decay, and electroweak Kaluza--Klein (KK) resonances in a dark-dimension-inspired interval model. The gravitational length sets the five-dimensional Planck scale, while a shorter gauge interval controls the KK spectrum and the stretched-state mass. We construct normalized fermion and Higgs profiles, diagonalize the neutral-vector sector, and determine its fermionic widths. Proton partial lifetimes are evaluated using a two-operator, SU(5)-inspired effective matching prescription. One-loop four-dimensional MSSM and split-supersymmetric reference running determines electroweak coupling-crossing scales and the residual strong-coupling mismatch. A selected common-threshold benchmark gives a heavy-state mass of $1.137\times10^{16}$ GeV, a reference crossing of $1.139\times10^{16}$ GeV, and a conditional proton partial lifetime of $8.72\times10^{35}$ years. At a micron-scale gravitational length, suppressed baryon-violating matching amplitudes can satisfy proton limits, although the high-scale mass-matching condition selects a distinct region of the scanned geometry. Independently, a $5$ TeV neutral-vector benchmark yields an inclusive leading-order dielectron cross section of $0.183$ fb over $4.5$--$5.5$ TeV at a collider energy of $13.6$ TeV, before detector selection. The analysis provides quantitative effective-model benchmarks and identifies the remaining high-scale matching and experimental tests.

title: Cosmological Correlators with Triple Massive Exchanges
abstract: Among all tree-level contributions to the primordial bispectrum, the triple exchange of massive scalars is the most challenging. In this paper we present an analytical formula for this bispectrum in the form of a double series, which allows the three exchanged fields to have different masses and converges throughout the whole physical region. We obtain it by expanding the mixed propagator with the softest momentum, so that the triple exchange becomes a sum of integrals over two mixed propagators. Each of these integrals satisfies a differential equation and is fixed by its value at equal momentum. We further show that the squeezed limit follows directly from this formula and takes a simple and compact form.

title: Analysis of the triply-charm tetraquark states via the QCD sum rules
abstract: In this work, we construct the diquark-antidiquark type local currents to interpolate the triply-charm tetraquark states, and investigate the spectroscopy of the scalar, axialvector and tensor triply-charm tetraquark states via the QCD sum rules comprehensively. As a byproduct, we obtain the masses of four vector triply-charm tetraquark states.

title: Chromatic calorimetry using nanocomposites: status and future challenges
abstract: The development of advanced detector technologies will play a key role in future high-energy physics experiments, such as the FCC-ee. In this context, chromatic calorimetry is an emerging concept for electromagnetic calorimeters, with the potential to combine the precise energy measurement of homogeneous calorimeters with longitudinal reconstruction of particle showers. The state of the art in chromatic calorimetry is reviewed, including experimental results from proof-of-concept prototypes and simulation studies investigating quantum-dot-based configurations. Recent progress and current challenges in the development of nanocomposites are also discussed. Finally, future prospects for chromatic calorimetry are outlined.

title: Zeroing in on BSM at Colliders
abstract: Destructive interference between light and heavy dynamics can produce a zero in the amplitude which, for strongly coupled UV completions, lies parametrically below the heavy threshold. We identify under which assumptions this parametrically light zero exists, and when it admits an effective field theory description. We study how absorptive effects and helicity structure affect the existence of the zero and turn it into a dip. When the dip is kinematically accessible, we show how its position, depth, and curvature constrain the UV dynamics. Collider examples illustrate the importance of interference in indirect searches and the information available when the zero is kinematically accessible.

title: A pseudoscalar Higgs boson interfering with toponium: a QCD analysis of $\mathbf{gg\to A\to t\bar t}$ near threshold
abstract: The CMS and ATLAS collaborations have observed an excess of $t\bar t$ events near threshold that is consistent with the formation of the pseudoscalar toponium state $\eta_t$. A pseudoscalar Higgs boson $A$ with a large coupling to top quarks could contribute part of this excess and the presence of the $A$ boson could be concealed. We point out that, if such a state exists with $M_A$ close to $2m_t$, it necessarily interferes with toponium, since both live in the colour--singlet ${}^1S_0$ channel and share the same Coulomb final--state interaction. Using exact leading--order amplitudes, whose relative phase is fixed by unitarity, and Coulomb resummation applied coherently to the QCD background, the $A$ boson signal and their interference, we show that the line shape is controlled by a single complex number $\kappa$, the ratio of the resonant and non--resonant amplitudes at the peak. Unitarity fixes ${\rm Im}\,\kappa=-1$ exactly when $A$ decays into top quarks, so that the interference reduces the resonant rate by $2/|\kappa|^2$ and produces an exact zero of the ${}^1S_0$ amplitude just above $M_A$. The parameter $\kappa$ does not depend on the $A$ coupling to top quarks and, with the Coulomb--enhanced width we find $|\kappa|\approx1.5$--$1.7$ for $M_A=350$--$380$ GeV and, hence, the $A$ resonance is completely distorted. For an $A$ boson accounting for 50\% (25\%) of the observed excess, it enhances the toponium peak by about 10 to 70\% (5 to 35\%), and the threshold excess differs strongly from the sum of the toponium and $A$ contributions.

title: Quark dipole operators in the gradient-flow scheme at NNLO QCD
abstract: Conversion factors for the dimension-five QCD operator basis from the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ to the gradient-flow scheme are presented through NNLO in the strong coupling. In the CP-even sector, the results are provided for general quark masses and arbitrary flavor content of the operators. Specifically, this concerns the quark CMDM operator and its mixing with lower-dimensional QCD operators. In the massless case, our results immediately apply to the quark chromoelectric dipole operator. As a by-product, we also determine missing entries in the $\overline{\textrm{MS}}$ anomalous dimension matrix of the CMDM operator to NNLO QCD.

title: Challenging the K\"orner-Pati-Woo Theorem in Charmed Baryon Decays
abstract: The K\"orner-Pati-Woo (KPW) theorem is a long-standing selection rule widely used in heavy-baryon decays. In this work, we argue that the conventional valence-color argument underlying the KPW theorem does not, by itself, establish an exact selection rule. The $\rm KPW$-$\rm SU(3)_F$ prediction for $\mathcal{B}(\Xi_c^0\to pK^-)$, inferred from $\Lambda_c^+\to \Xi^0K^+$, is $17.2\pm6.0$ times the measured value. A joint likelihood fit to five observables in $\Xi_c^0\to pK^-$ and $\Lambda_c^+\to \Xi^0K^+$ yields a $6.3\sigma$ discrepancy under the $\rm KPW$-$\rm SU(3)_F$ ansatz. A comparison of $\alpha(\Lambda_c^+\to \Delta^{++}K^-)$ and $\alpha(\Lambda_c^+\to \Sigma^{*}\pi)$ reveals a pronounced sign-sensitive tension. Accommodating these measurements within the KPW constraint requires anomalously large $\rm SU(3)_F$ breaking effects. Future measurements of $\Lambda^+_c\to\Sigma^{(*)0}K^+$, $\Sigma^{(*)+}K^0_S$, $\Delta^+\eta^{(\prime)}$, $\Delta^{++}\pi^-$, $\Delta^+\pi^0$, $\Delta^0\pi^+$, $\Delta^{++}K^-$, and $\Delta^{+}K^0_S$ would provide high-precision tests of the KPW theorem.

title: Balancing heavy flavour: Quantum number compensation in the hadronisation of charm and beauty particles in proton-proton collisions
abstract: The hadronisation of heavy quarks remains one of the least understood processes of Quantum Chromodynamics (QCD). While the production of heavy quark pairs can be calculated perturbatively in QCD, the subsequent formation of hadrons involves non-perturbative processes. The description of these processes is predominantly model dependent and sensitive to the underlying mechanisms of colour reconnection and string fragmentation. In particular, the conservation of flavour, baryon number and charge imposes constraints on how heavy-flavour hadrons are formed and balanced within the final state. In this work, we study how the quantum numbers associated with charm and beauty production are balanced in proton-proton collisions, using events simulated with the PYTHIA-8 event generator. Starting from perturbatively produced ($c\overline{c}$) and ($b\overline{b}$) pairs, we examine how the formation of heavy-flavour mesons and baryons, including $D^0$, $B^+$, $\Lambda_c^+$, and $\Lambda_b^0$, is accompanied by compensating particles elsewhere. The analysis focuses on correlations between the identified heavy hadron and the hadronic system responsible for balancing its conserved quantum numbers. We compare three hadronisation configurations that are implemented in PYTHIA: the Monash tune, colour-reconnection models incorporating string junctions (SJ), and close-packing (CP) approaches. We find that the SJ and CP tunes show a substantially enhanced contribution of baryons to the charm and beauty balancing yields compared with the Monash tune; this enhancement becomes more pronounced in high-multiplicity events. This study introduces a framework for characterising quantum-number compensation in heavy-flavour production and provides a new way to test hadronisation dynamics using identified charm- and beauty-hadron correlations, which can be explored at current and future collider experiments.

title: Quantifying the TKM-IKT ambiguity: translating the theoretical benchmark into experimental discriminants for future colliders
abstract: This paper, the second of two companion works, translates the theoretical benchmark established in into quantitative predictions for high-energy $\gamma\gamma$ interactions. We simultaneously confront the TKM and IKT dipole cross-section prescriptions across five representative saturation models (GBW, IIMS, rcBK, AGBS, WYKWC). Evaluating real and virtual cross sections, $F_2^\gamma$, and heavy-quark production, we demonstrate that the TKM--IKT discrepancy is an irreducible structural ambiguity reaching $48\pm12\%$ at LEP energies and expanding into the TeV regime. We propose three experimental discriminants for future colliders (ILC, CLIC, FCC-ee) --- emphasizing exclusive $\gamma\gamma \to J/\psi + J/\psi$ production where quadratic amplitude scaling ($[\mathcal{N}]^2$) magnifies the divergence --- elevating these comparisons from parameter choices to rigorous falsification tests of the foundational premises. Finally, an analytical universality test using GBW DIS parameters establishes the quantitative baseline required to falsify the underlying dipole--target analogy.

title: Soft-photon resummation for low-energy $e^+e^-$ colliders
abstract: We present resummed predictions for $e^+e^- \to \mu^+\mu^-(\gamma)$ and $\pi^+\pi^-(\gamma)$ in the multi-photon soft limit, matched to exact NLO. The resummation is performed within the Yennie-Frautschi-Suura framework at the amplitude level. The initial and final-state contributions are included coherently, and NLO accuracy with finite electron, muon and pion masses is achieved. We present our calculation, its implementation in a fast Fortran Monte Carlo integrator, and compare our predictions with the generators BabaYaga, KKMC, Phokhara and McMule, in scenarios inspired by the energy-scan (CMD) and radiative-return (KLOE, BES III, B factories) experiments. We find agreement with BabaYaga, which includes higher-order corrections through a parton shower, at the per-mille level in the cross-sections, and differences of up to two percent with the soft-photon resummation of KKMC. This work represents an important step towards the validation of Monte Carlo generators for low-energy experiments, and will be released in the upcoming new version of Phokhara.

title: Probing CP violation in weak radiative and dielectron decays of $\Lambda$ and $\Xi^-$ hyperons
abstract: The rare decays $\Lambda\to ne^+e^-$ and $\Xi^-\to\Sigma^-e^+e^-$ can serve as sensitive probes of $CP$ violation, especially that induced by interactions from beyond the standard model. We demonstrate that this is so because the dominant long-distance components of these processes provide sizable absorptive phases that can give rise to significant $CP$ violation via interference with potential new-physics effects. Treating the new contributions model-independently, we find that this leads to $CP$-odd rate asymmetries that are currently allowed by kaon and hyperon data to reach the 10% and 20% levels in the $\Lambda$ and $\Xi^-$ cases, respectively. Interestingly, we obtain comparable outcomes for the related weak radiative modes $\Lambda\to n\gamma$ and $\Xi^-\to\Sigma^-\gamma$. These results are testable at future high-statistics hyperon facilities.

title: Is Neutrino Disappearance Sensitive to T-Violation for Asymmetric Matter Profiles ?
abstract:
It is commonly stated in the literature that T violation is zero in neutrino disappearance channels. We show this claim is not general: it holds only for symmetric matter profiles or when the T/CP-violating phase ($\delta$) is 0 or $\pi$, that is, when the Jarlskog invariant is zero. The $
u_\mu$ and $
u_	au$, but not the $
u_e$, survival probabilities carry a $\sin\delta$-dependent term that is non-zero in asymmetric matter and constitutes a genuine T asymmetry. The confusion arises from an improper T test that subtracts a probability from itself: a mathematical identity, not a physics result. In this paper, we clarify the distinctions between a proper and an improper T test as well as the proper and improper CP and CPT tests, for a general, arbitrary matter profile. For a toy model consisting of two different layers of constant density, we find that the maximum T-violation is obtained when one layer is close to the solar resonance, and the other is close to the atmospheric resonance. We address whether the matter asymmetry for DUNE and Hyper-Kamiokande experiments is sufficiently large to allow the $\sin\delta$ dependence to be probed in $
u_\mu$ survival probability. We also discuss future experimental scenarios that could probe T/CP-violation in $
u_\mu$ survival probability.

title: Ohmic warm inflation
abstract: We show that Warm Little Inflation is anomalous, lacks a suitable inflaton potential, and cannot sustain the thermal bath, as the quasi-static approximation over-estimated the dissipated power. To address these issues, we propose a new friction mechanism and new anomaly-free models based on one fermion charged under a U(1) gauge group in one extra dimension. The four-dimensional lattice version is a ring of $N$ U(1) groups with one fermion at each site, reducing to an anomaly-free version of the warm little inflaton model for $N=2$. The inflaton is a Wilson line, protected for $N\ge5$. Large $N$ allows a suitable monodromy inflaton potential. In the continuum limit, $N\to\infty$, the inflaton velocity becomes a five-dimensional electric field and friction becomes Ohmic dissipation, which seems able to sustain warm inflation compatibly with observations.
